title: DNA Analysis by Native Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis
author: Michael Van Dyke
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.mcyc2xw
materials: We routinely use the Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN® vertical electrophoresis system to cast and run 10-well 1.0 mm-thick 9.5%:0.5% polyacrylamide:bisacrylamide minigels in ½X TBE buffer [44.5 mM Tris base, 44.5 mM boric acid, 1 mM EDTA]. Needed materials: Bio-Rad casting stand, two casting frames, two short plates, two 1.0 mm spacer plates, two 1.0 mm 10-well combs, and one Mini-PROTEAN® vertical electrophoresis cell with buffer dam. Needed reagents: 5x TBE buffer, 38:2 acrylamide:bisacrylamide, 10% ammonium persulfate (APS), and tetramethylenediamine (TEMED), all stored at 4 ºC. a

To assemble the gel casting apparatus, place a short plate on top of a spacer plate. Note that there is an internal space between the two and the writing on the spacer plate is exposed at the top of the sandwich. a Slide the two plates into an unlocked casting frame (clamps forward) from the top while on a level surface, making sure the short plate is oriented to the front of the frame. With the plates and frame flush with the level surface, lock the assembly by rotating the clamps 90º from their forward to their outward position. Check by hand to ensure both plates and frame are flush at the bottom. Repeat procedure if not. a Place the entire assembly onto a Bio-Rad casting frame with the short plate forward and the casting frame seated with its base back touching the casting stand. Lock the plate/casting stand in place by engaging the spring-loaded lever on the top of the casting stand and applying pressure to the top of the spacer plate with the short plate oriented forward. Now it is ready for gel casting. a

steps.title: Cast two 10% minigels
steps.instruction: Prepare two 10% polyacrylamide minigels by mixing reagents, polymerizing, and inserting the comb.

substeps.instruction: Add to a 15 mL screw‑cap centrifuge tube in order: 7.8 mL water, 1.2 mL 5X TBE, 3.0 mL 38:2 acrylamide:bis, and 45 µL 10 % APS.
Vortex briefly to mix.
Add 15 µL TEMED, vortex briefly again.
Load the gel solution into each of the two casting assemblies using a 6 in. Pasteur pipette, stopping 2 mm from the top.
Insert a 10‑well comb at a slight angle to avoid air bubbles and seat it completely.
Allow free‑radical polymerization to complete for 15 min at room temperature; gels are ready for use thereafter.

steps.title: Store minigels for later use
steps.instruction: Keep cast minigels hydrated and refrigerated to preserve them for up to one month.

substeps.instruction: Minigels in their casting stands can remain at room temperature/humidity for several hours without issue.
For long‑term storage, add ~200 µL water to the comb/small plate junction, wrap the stand in plastic or place it in an airtight container, and store at 4 °C.
Properly stored gels remain functional for at least one month.

steps.title: Assemble gel in Mini-PROTEAN tank
steps.instruction: Secure the minigel (and buffer dam if used) in the electrophoresis tank and fill with ½X TBE buffer.

substeps.instruction: Place one polyacrylamide minigel and one buffer dam on each side of the Mini‑PROTEAN® electrode assembly, ensuring the green gasket “ears” fully seal with the plate/spacer junction and the plastic lip of the buffer dam.
Close the side clamps and insert the assembly into the tank.
Prepare 500 mL ½X TBE buffer.
Fill the central chamber with ½X TBE and observe for leakage; if leakage occurs, drain, reseat the gel and buffer dam, and refill.
If running two gels simultaneously, substitute the second buffer dam with a second minigel.

steps.title: Prepare DNA loading samples
steps.instruction: Make DNA samples with appropriate glucose and Orange G loading dye concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Ensure each sample total volume does not exceed 12 µL and contains at least 3.3 % glucose and 0.025 % Orange G (final concentrations).
For a 5 µL binding reaction, add 1 µL 6X Orange Loading Dye (20 % glucose, 0.15 % Orange G, stored at –20 °C).
Mix thoroughly by repeated pipetting.

steps.title: Load samples and connect electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Dispense samples into wells, add buffer, and attach the power leads with correct polarity.

substeps.instruction: Load each sample into its well using a P10 Pipetman with 0.1–10 µL tips.
After all samples are loaded, add ½X TBE buffer to the bottom chamber.
Seat the tank lid.
Attach the leads to the power‑supply, ensuring the lid‑to‑electrode assembly and lead‑to‑socket orientations give the proper electrode polarity.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis with voltage program
steps.instruction: Electrophorese the gel using a two‑step voltage protocol and then clean the apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Apply constant voltage of 5 V/cm (50 V) for 5 min to let DNA enter the gel.
Increase voltage to 10 V/cm (100 V) for the remainder of the run (≈1 h) to move Orange G near the bottom (~10 bp dsDNA).
When the run finishes, drain the tank and electrode assembly, wash with water, and disassemble.
Do not separate the gel plates; they can be imaged directly.
Use a power supply with an integrated timer for reproducibility, and avoid leaving gels at room temperature for extended periods to prevent diffusion of short DNA fragments.

steps.title: Prepare imager and place gel
steps.instruction: Clean the imaging surface and position the gel sandwich for scanning.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the imager glass surface with DI water and Kimwipes™ until completely clean.
Place the gel sandwich on the glass with the short‑plate face down.
Align the gel with both axes so that its location matches the template in Image Studio™.
Close the imager lid.

steps.title: Perform preview and full scan
steps.instruction: Acquire a quick preview to set intensity, then run the full image acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Set intensity to 4 for both 700 nm and 800 nm channels and run a preview scan (~30 s).
Adjust intensity up or down as needed until no saturated (white) pixels are observed.
Start the full scan (approximately 8.5 min).

steps.title: Save acquired images
steps.instruction: Export the scanned images in desired formats and resolutions.

substeps.instruction: Save images as tif, png, or jpg files at 150, 300, or 600 dpi; the standard is a 600 dpi jpg.
Adjust gain for each channel using the Curves box if needed (note that gain changes visual appearance but not quantitation).

steps.title: Manually quantify bands
steps.instruction: Use the analysis tools to draw rectangles around bands and background for pixel quantitation.

substeps.instruction: Open the Analysis tab in Image Studio™.
Select Shape → Draw Rectangle and enclose each band or background region, keeping all rectangles the same dimensions.
Quantify one channel at a time; both channels can be displayed simultaneously after analysis.

steps.title: Record quantification values
steps.instruction: Display pixel numbers, note channel colors, and save the final annotated image.

substeps.instruction: Click Show → Quantification to view pixel numbers for each band; the color bar indicates the channel (700 or 800).
Save the final image that includes the quantification values.
If necessary, reduce channel gain to improve visibility; pixel numbers remain unchanged.

steps.title: Infrared fluorescence imaging (IRF)
steps.instruction: Set up the LI‑COR Odyssey and Image Studio™ for IR‑labeled DNA imaging.

substeps.instruction: Use a LI‑COR Odyssey imager with Image Studio™ 5.2.
Select the DNA preset and set Scan Controls: Scan Resolution 84 µm, Scan Quality Medium, Focus Offset 1.5 mm, Flip Image.
Choose a 7 × 9 cm grid covering the minigel (typically the leftmost, bottom corner).
Enable the appropriate IRDye® channels for the labeled DNA.
Set initial intensity based on DNA amount: 10 fmol → Intensity 9; 100 fmol → Intensity 6; 1000 fmol → Intensity 3.
